CHEMISTRY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The Mole.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Mole.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole.

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.

11. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
